channel.title: France 24 - International breaking news, top stories and headlines
channel.description: Breaking news and world news from France 24 on Business, Sports, Culture. Video news. News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America

item.title: Trump and Xi meet, but hopes for AI cooperation stay slim
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump have been holding talks in the Oval Office at the White House today. President Donald Trump gave the visiting leader of communist China a personal tour of several of his favorite White House features. He took him aboard the Marine One helicopter, presented the new granite landing pad he had built for it, and pointed out the massive adjacent construction site where a ballroom will eventually stand.
item.dc:creator: Yinka OYETADE

item.title: ‘Send in the Clowns’: Viral video fuels claims Denmark trolled Trump and Rubio
item.description: A viral video claims Danish officials played Judy Collins’ “Send in the Clowns” as US Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrived for a Greenland signing ceremony, sparking claims of Danish “trolling”. Our checks of separate livestreams confirm the song really played and the video was not manipulated. Denmark has denied choosing the music, while the UN says it did not organise the event. Whilst the song was real, there is no evidence Denmark selected it deliberately. Vedika Bahl fact-checks.
item.dc:creator: Vedika BAHL

item.title: Macron says 'CIA did not ​inform French services' of possible Russian drone attacks
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron on Thursday denied a report by Spanish newspaper El Mundo that the US Central Intelligence Agency had warned European governments of possible Russian drone attacks from the Mediterranean. He also said in a primetime TV interview that France will send troops and defence systems to Saudi Arabia to help protect the Red Sea port city of Yanbu.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Iran sees air, land travel chaos as US sanctions bite
item.description: Flights between Iran and the United Arab Emirates have been suspended, following tighter US sanctions on Iran's aviation industry. The move effectively cuts Tehran off from Dubai, one of the region's most important commercial hubs. There are also huge backups near Iran's border with Turkey, as overland shipping routes struggle to fill the gaps. Also in this edition - Donald Trump and Xi Jinping hail strong ties between the US and China as they discuss AI, trade, and energy.
item.dc:creator: Kate MOODY

item.title: Tigray rebels in 'full-blown' war with government
item.description: In tonight's edition, Tigrayans in northern Ethiopia start panic buying supplies in the rush to stock up amidst fears that months of tensions have finally tipped over into full-blown conflict. Also, power cuts return to Senegal. And Yemis Alade, the Nigerian superstar, is out with a new album and speaks to France 24.
item.dc:creator: Georja CALVIN-SMITH

item.title: Israeli PM Netanyahu calls Gaza genocide allegations ‘biggest lie of the century’
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu gave a combative speech at the UN General Assembly on Thursday in which he denied that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza, lashed out at leaders, including New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani, and said attacking Iran was "one of the easiest decisions" he had ever made.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: REPLAY: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu speaks at the UNGA
item.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on ​Thursday mounted a forceful defense of Israel's actions in the region at the UN, seeking to counter growing international isolation ahead of elections he could lose, as dozens of delegates streamed out.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: The future of AI in their hands? Trump-Xi summit dismisses calls for global oversight
item.description: It’s their AI world and we’re just living in it. If that's the feeling of those who suffer from AI anxiety, it may worsen watching the Chinese president’s first state visit to Washington in nine years. If there's one issue where the planet's biggest superpowers agree on, it's now’s not the time for global regulation of artificial intelligence. As they sit down to a White House dinner hours after news that OpenAI had hacked the Australian government, we’ll ask who will call to task the US tech titans at the table.
item.dc:creator: François PICARD

item.title: Residents in West Bank's Masafer Yatta face Israeli demolitions
item.description: On September 2, the Israeli army demolished the village of Khirbet a-Taban in the occupied West Bank. The village is located in Masafer Yatta, an area Israel declared a restricted military zone. Residents of the area have been reporting an increase in demolitions by the Israeli army and harassment by Israeli settlers since the October 7 Hamas attack.
item.dc:creator: The FRANCE 24 Observers

item.title: 🔴 Live: ‘We’re going to win because we’ve got no other choice’, Israeli PM Netanyahu says at UN
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Israeli policies threaten 'life and existence' of Palestinians, Abbas tells UN
item.description: Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas addressed the UN General Assembly on Thursday by video after being denied a visa to the United States for the second year in a row. In his prerecorded speech, he denounced Israeli policies that he said threatened Palestinians with a new Nakba and vowed that his people would remain “on their land”.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Schism with rebel Catholic sect casts a pall over Pope Leo’s visit to France
item.description: The Vatican’s recent excommunication of followers of a Catholic splinter sect, the Society of Saint Pius X, has revived a longstanding feud within the Roman Catholic Church ahead of Pope Leo XIV’s state visit to France. The ultra-conservative group has established an extensive network of schools and has attracted thousands of followers in France.
item.dc:creator: Bahar MAKOOI

item.title: Threat to 'life and existence': Major takeaways from Palestinian president's UN speech
item.description: Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas addressed the UN General Assembly on Thursday, delivering prerecorded remarks from his office in Ramallah after the United States denied him and other top Palestinian officials visas to attend the gathering for the second year in a row. “The Palestinian people face one of the most dangerous times in its history,” Abbas said. France 24's Kethevane Gorjestani takes a look at some of the main takeaways from his address.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: REPLAY: Palestinian president Abbas addresses UN General Assembly
item.description: Palestinian president Mahmud Abbas told the UN on Thursday that Israeli policies no longer just jeopardized a two-state solution but were now threatening the "very life and existence" of his people. Abbas delivered prerecorded remarks to the UN’s General Assembly from his office in Ramallah after the United States denied him and other top Palestinian officials visas to attend the gathering for the second year in a row.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: How do the French feel about religion?
item.description: Amid the enthusiasm over the first papal visit to France in 18 years, we take a deep dive into religion in France. We try to answer the question, "How do the French feel about religion?" From its Catholic heritage to laïcité, or secularism, we break down the statistics on the French people's relationship to faith.
item.dc:creator: Solange MOUGIN

item.title: 'Trump views US-China relations as a personal friendship: Xi views US as an adversary to be managed'
item.description: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Henrietta Levin, Senior Fellow with the Freeman Chair in China Studies at the Center for Strategic and International Studies in Washington. The US remains a powerful actor in its relationship with China. But power on paper is not the same thing as leverage at the negotiating table. Levin warns that President Trump’s highly personalized approach to Xi Jinping offers Beijing opportunities that China can easily exploit. Xi does not approach the relationship in the same way. Au contraire, he sees the United States as an adversary to be managed while China pursues its domestic priorities and strategic objectives in Asia, including on Taiwan.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: United States: Trump's unconventional welcome for Xi's state visit
item.description: 🇺🇸 🇨🇳 In a first for a US president, Donald Trump greeted his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping on the tarmac as the latter landed in a military airbase near Washington DC on Wednesday for a three-day state visit.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: 🔴 Live: Palestinian President Abbas calls on UN General Assembly to 'not allow another Nakba'
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Nigerian superstar Yemi Alade: From viral hit 'Johnny' to working with Beyoncé
item.description: Nigerian superstar Yemi Alade is one of Africa's biggest female artists, with global hits, hundreds of millions of views online and a collaboration with Beyoncé. Speaking to Eve Jackson as she kicks off her new tour, the Grammy-nominated singer looks back on her remarkable career, reveals how she nearly missed the email that led to her "Black Is King" collaboration with Beyoncé and talks about her new album, "It's Yemi Alade", and latest single "Ala Bekee" with Don Jazzy.
item.dc:creator: Eve JACKSON

item.title: Kévi Donat, founder of Le Paris Noir: 'Paris is much more diverse than perhaps people expect'
item.description: The man behind a company that aims to put the stories of Black men and women back at the heart of Paris where they belong has spoken to FRANCE 24 about his mission. Kévi Donat came up with the idea of Le Paris Noir – an agency providing tours in Paris that follow in the historical footsteps of major Black figures to tell their real stories.
item.dc:creator: Stuart NORVAL

item.title: EU sanctions Russian pundit Xenia Fedorova after expulsion from France
item.description: The European Union on Thursday imposed sanctions on Russian commentator Xenia Fedorova, whom France expelled in August over claims that she was disseminating "pro-Russian narratives" in the country.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: The French Senate: Old, expensive and out of touch or necessary safeguard to democracy?
item.description: France is gearing up for an election this Sunday, September 27 to renew just about half of the Senate's 348 red velvet seats. The French parliament is the country's bicameral legislature. The lower house (the National Assembly) tends to overshadow the upper house (the Senate). So what does the Senate actually do? Is it a powerful protector of the regions or a retirement club for old, mostly male politicians? We take a closer look in French Connections.
item.dc:creator: Florence VILLEMINOT

item.title: 🔴 CNN, MS NOW, Politico still barred from White House despite court ruling
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Taiwan: Home of semiconductor giants at the centre of AI race
item.description: The topic of artificial intelligence looms large as Chinese President Xi Jinping begins his highly anticipated state visit to Washington. The fate of Taiwan – coveted by its larger neighbour, China – will also be on the table. It's the global leader in superconductor research and development. These powerful chips can be found in smartphones, computers, and above all in AI development. Our France 2 colleagues take a rare look inside one of Taiwan's state-of-the-art laboratories.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 2
